name: Advanced Micro Devices
description: AMD designs processors and accelerators but does not manufacture them; it pays outside foundries to make them. Its largest business sells EPYC server CPUs and Instinct AI GPUs to data centers; it also sells Ryzen PC processors, Radeon graphics and custom chips for game consoles, and programmable chips for embedded systems. Each is a chip-by-chip sale to PC makers, cloud providers and console makers. The AI business is the growth driver: Data Center revenue was $6.7B in Q2 2026, more than double the year-earlier quarter.

gics.note: Conventional GICS label (sector and sub-industry) read from Wikipedia, List of S&P 500 companies, on 2026-09-30 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_S%26P_500_companies). That page gives only sector and sub-industry; industry group and industry are null because no source read states them. Labelled conventional filing only; Mowgli classification is not assigned here.

hq.note: 2485 Augustine Drive, Santa Clara, CA 95054 (SEC EDGAR business address)

businessLines.name: Data Center
businessLines.how: Hyperscalers and server makers buy processors and AI GPUs per unit under multi-year roadmaps; AI GPU revenue depends on large customer deployment programs (for example a 6-gigawatt OpenAI agreement, first gigawatt on MI450).
businessLines.description: EPYC server CPUs, Instinct GPUs (MI200, MI300, MI325, MI350 series), DPUs, AI NICs, and FPGA/adaptive SoCs for servers.

businessLines.name: Client and Gaming
businessLines.how: PC processors sold per chip to PC makers and channel; console chips are custom parts sold to console makers, so revenue follows the console cycle and is lumpy (Gaming down 31% in Q2 2026).
businessLines.description: Client (Ryzen PC processors), Gaming (Radeon discrete graphics and semi-custom console chips).

businessLines.name: Embedded
businessLines.how: Programmable and embedded chips designed into long-life products (factory, network, vehicle); sold per unit after a multi-year design win.
businessLines.description: Embedded CPUs and APUs, FPGAs, adaptive SoCs, and SOMs for communications, industrial, automotive and other uses.

brands.name: ZT Systems (acquired; total consideration $4.4B: $3.2B cash, $860M stock, $361M contingent)
brands.segment: AI and compute infrastructure; a manufacturing business was divested (heading in the Q2 2026 10-Q)

whatsNext.text: OpenAI to deploy 6 gigawatts of AMD GPUs; first gigawatt on Instinct MI450. OpenAI warrant (exercisable to 2030-10-05) and Meta warrant (exercisable to 2031-02-23) each cover up to 160 million shares at $0.01, vesting on GPU purchase milestones and stock price targets; none vested as of 2026-06-27.
